source: You decided to destroy a section of the journals.
This are your personal thoughts from the last six months. Every peaceful moment in the tent, captured here - every last doubt and worry, put down into words.
A paragraph of the entry seems almost thankful to HQ - the wastes were clearly as hostile and lifeless as you were told they'd be.
You rip the page from the journal, leaving a jagged strip of paper between the other pages. It's mostly unnoticeable, but who knows.
The next section was about your thoughts on the wastes, but the page has since been ripped out.
The following page specified which of you were the driving force behind the experiments, but you tore out that page moments ago.
The next part of the same entry specifies which one of you were the driving force behind the experiments - Jorge.
The next part of the same entry specifies which one of you were the driving force behind the experiments - you.
You carefully tear out the page, taking care to leave as little trace of it as possible. You cover it up fairly well.
You tore out the following page earlier - the one containing some of your thoughts on HQ.
The first entry that catches your eye is the one you made the morning of the discovery. It describes your concerns and excitement about the future of your work.
The next page, still from the same entry, contains some choice words regarding HQ - mostly about their ineptitude.
What follows are your thoughts on HQ - nothing too critical, and some of it even positive.
Pressing your thumb against the gutter between the pages, you slowly tear out the page in question.
The next few pages are blank. There's room for a few more entries - or at the very least, one for tomorrow morning.
The next entry of note that you find is far more colorful - written in the morning before you began experimenting on the artifact.
You open up the journal again. It couldn't hurt to have another look, could it?
A brief passage describes your disillusionment with what HQ told you - the wastes are clearly not as lifeless as you were led to believe, and your superiors lied.
